note: Literature confirms LGMDR29 caused by biallelic SNUPN variants is characterized by a limb-girdle muscular dystrophy phenotype with proximal weakness typically presenting in childhood or young adulthood.

evidence.text: Patients with biallelic variants in SNUPN presented with limb-girdle muscular dystrophy characterized by proximal weakness starting in childhood, restrictive respiratory dysfunction, and prominent contractures.

source.title: Biallelic variants in SNUPN cause a limb girdle muscular dystrophy with myofibrillar-like features
source.quote: SNUPN patients show a similar phenotype characterized by proximal weakness starting in childhood, restrictive respiratory dysfunction and prominent contractures, although inter-individual variability in terms of severity even in individuals from the same family was found.

numbers.metric: affected patients from unrelated families evaluated

evidence.text: LGMDR29 covers a spectrum ranging from childhood-onset muscular dystrophy to adult-onset proximo-distal and axial muscle weakness with early respiratory impairment.

source.title: SNUPN‐Related Muscular Dystrophy: Novel Phenotypic, Pathological and Functional Protein Insights
source.quote: SNUPN-related muscular dystrophy or LGMDR29 is a new entity that covers from a congenital or childhood onset pure muscular dystrophy to more complex phenotypes combining neurodevelopmental features, cataracts, or spinocerebellar ataxia.
